label: text
text: The national delegate conference of the Miners' Federation sat all day long, heard reports from the districts, and discussed the Government's proposals. The delegates were evidently divided on the matter and adjourned till tomorrow when Mr. A. J. Cook and other officials expect to fly to Ostend to attend a meeting of the International Miners' Federation when the question of an international strike will be discussed.

label: text
text: Mr. Cock, in a speech in the Memorial Hall, London, to-night, complained that the Government had tricked the miners. The Government's proposals were degrading and tantamount to terms of surrender, to which the miners' leaders to-day said what the men would say next week, namely, "No."—Reuter

label: text
text: According to the coal owners' figures 8,000 more miners have returned in various districts today, including 750 at Atherton, where the miners balloted in favour of resumption at practically pre-stoppage wages for a 7½-hour's day.—Reuter.

label: text
text: That the drifting back of the miners towards work is accelerating is evidenced by the fact that over 10,000 more returned to work yesterday evening, making the total, including safety men, over 160,000 out of a million miners normally employed.—Reuter...

label: paragraph_title
text: Not Yet Found by the Miners.

label: text
text: The centre of gravity in the coal dispute lay to-day in the conference of the miners' delegates. Their deliberations were conducted behind closed doors.

label: text
text: According to official statements the conference unanimously endorsed the actions of the Miners' Executive in their latest negotiations with the Government, and proceeded to discuss the Government's proposals.

label: text
text: This discussion occupied the whole afternoon, and the conference adjourned until to-morrow, when the Government's proposals will be further considered.

label: text
text: From interviews with various delegates the impression was obtained that, "whilst there was a section in favour of a fight to finish, the majority of the delegates were anxious for some kind of way out. This feeling was evidently not lessened by the reports of an increasing resumption of work in the coal fields.

label: text
text: The opinion was commonly held that the conference would eventually refer the Government's proposals to the districts. It was suggested that there was a possibility that before the conference took this step, it might recommend the Executive to seek a further interview at Downing Street, to see if a formula could be discovered which would enable the Government to suggest a meeting between the miners and the owners on the basis of a compromise between the Government's offer and the Mining Federation's proposals.

label: text
text: As a matter of fact the Prime Minister remained at 10 Downing Street the whole of the day in case either of the parties in the coal dispute might desire to see him—British Wireless Service.

Vera Cruz, Sept. '29:
The Hurricane lasted several hours, its velocity being 125 miles an hour.

label: text
text: The damage is estimated a $2,500,000 but no fatalities have so far been reported.

label: text
text: The crops in the vicinity of Vera Cruz were ruined and damage was also done at Boca del Rio, Cordoba, and Pasco del Macho.

label: text
text: Two persons were drowned in the floods at Jalapa.—Reuter.

label: text
text: The destruction of communications is responsible for very meagre details up to the present, but reports from Vera Cruz describe the hurricane of yesterday as "worst since the famous storm of 1888.

label: text
text: Torrential rain fell for 24 hours and overflowed the Santiago River flooding the surrounding country whilst driven by the terrific gale enormous waves swept toward the shore and smashed the sea front.

label: text
text: Most of the city streets are three feet in water, flooding the lower parts of the buildings in the business quarter, the windows of which were shattered by the wind.

label: text
text: Lightly constructed houses in the residential sections suffered severely.—Reuter.

label: text
text: It is reported from Buenaventura (Colombia) that a cyclone caused great destruction to the Santa Marta banana plantations, and that the town of Cienega was damaged by floods.—Reuter's American Service.

label: text
text: Sir George Rowland Blades was to-day elected with traditional ceremonial to be Lord Mayor of London for the coming civic year.

label: text
text: Outside his business activities Sir G. Blades is known for his interest in cricket, having in his day been a first class player.—British Wireless Service.

label: text
text: [Sir George Rowland Blades, Bt., was born on April 15, 1868, being the son of Mr. Rowland Hill Blades, Sydenham, Kent. He has been Conservative M.P. for the Epsom Division of Surrey since 1918. He is Chairman of Blades, East and Blades, Ltd.; Alderman for the Ward of Bassishan, 1920; Senior Sheriff, City of London, 1917-18; J.P. for County of London, 1914, and Surrey, 1921; Hon. Colonel 54th (London) anti-Aircraft Brigade Royal Garrison Artillery; member of City of London Territorial Army Association; Military Member of Territorial Army Association of the County of Surrey; President of Surrey Provincial National Unionist Association; Almoner, Christ's Hospital; member of Court of Guy's Hospital; on Council of London Chamber of Commerce; on Committee of City of London Savings Association; and on Committee of Surrey County Cricket Club. His recreations are golf and cricket.

Ironwood (Michigan), Sept. 19.
"We are alive" were the welcome words heard by the reacting which, after a day's strenuous tunneling, succeeded in reaching the 20th level of the Pabst Iron Mine, where 48 miners have been entombed for over 120 hours as the result of "a cave in," which killed three of their comrades.

label: text
text: Doctors and ambulances have been rushed to the pit head ready to attend the men when they are brought to the surface—Reuter's American Service.

label: text
text: The Secretary of State Foreign Affairs, Sir Austin Chamberlain, who is spending his short holiday youchting in the Mediterranean, has accepted an invitation to meet Signor Musshi. The two statesmen are expected to take luncheon together to mrow probably at Civita Vecchia port near Rome.

label: text
text: The meeting is generally regarded as one of friendship and courtesy rather than of politic significance.---British Wireless Service.
